options.how: No enemies or raids: the pushback comes from zoning demand, traffic jams and service coverage you must balance.
Deadly cold and a coming storm; Hope and Discontent react to every law you sign in the Book of Laws.
Colony wealth feeds raid points, so getting richer draws bigger raids that test your defenses.

sources.note: Cities: Skylines: city builder about zoning, services and traffic
Frostpunk: developers on Hope, misery and the Book of Laws
RimWorld: colony wealth feeds raid points

options.how: No enemies: the pushback is market trends, review scores and cash flow as you choose topics and genres.
Heroes invade to loot your gold; your creatures and traps must repel them before they reach the Dungeon Heart.

sources.note: Game Dev Tycoon: run a game studio
Dungeon Keeper: heroes come for your gold; dig a dungeon with imps

options.how: Nothing attacks the park: pressure comes from guest happiness, queues, finances and scenery.
Infected hordes assault the colony; one breached wall can spread infection through every building.

sources.note: Planet Coaster: sandbox park builder, piece-by-piece construction
They Are Billions: infected hordes; build walls, gates and towers; survive a set period

options.how: No raiders: the colony is threatened by its own systems, running out of oxygen, overheating or stressing out.
The Greed attack at night, stealing coins and your crown unless walls and archers hold the line.

sources.note: Oxygen Not Included: threats are oxygen, temperature and stress
Kingdom Two Crowns: Greed attack at night; walls and towers defend

options.how: No enemies: the only opponent is space and adjacency, placing buildings for points to unlock the next island.
Harsh winters drain food and wood while wild creatures and rival clans attack your territory.

sources.note: Islanders: relaxing builder, placing buildings rewarded with points
Northgard: survive harsh winters and ferocious foes

options.how: No external threats: the challenge is animal welfare, habitat design and guest flow.
Tropical storms damage fences and dinosaurs escape, so ranger and capture teams must respond.

sources.note: Planet Zoo: animal welfare, habitats and a sandbox mode
Jurassic World Evolution: tropical storms and dinosaur escapes

options.how: You set work priorities and zones; colonists pick their own tasks from those priorities as their needs allow.
You till, water, harvest, mine and craft with your own avatar; sprinklers and Junimo huts automate only a little.

sources.note: RimWorld: Work tab priorities drive what colonists do
Stardew Valley: raise animals, tend crops, craft items yourself

options.how: Heroes have a will of their own: you cannot order them, only offer gold to persuade them to carry out your wishes.
You unpack deliveries, place goods on shelves, fridges and freezers, and scan items and take payment at the checkout yourself.

sources.note: Majesty: real-time strategy with indirect control, heroes have a will of their own and need gold to act
Supermarket Simulator: unpack goods, place them on shelves, scan items and take payments

options.how: You create jobs through designations, zones and work orders; idle dwarves with that labor enabled pick them up on their own.
Each player is a chef who must prepare, cook and serve every order by hand; nothing in the kitchen happens unless a chef does it.

sources.note: Dwarf Fortress: jobs come from designations and work orders; idle dwarves with the labor enabled take them
Dwarf Fortress: command dwarves with their own simulated personalities
Overcooked!: you and fellow chefs must prepare, cook and serve up orders

options.how: You build rooms and hire staff; doctors, nurses and handymen walk to jobs and treat patients on their own.
You run the kitchen with your own chef: chop, cook, plate and serve each order by hand, nothing happens unless you do it.

sources.note: Theme Hospital: design and manage a hospital from an empty building
Overcooked!: co-op kitchen orders

options.how: You lay blueprints and set regimes; hired workers build them and prisoners act on their own needs.
You prepare every order yourself, pressing a key per ingredient and step, then serve it before the customer leaves.

sources.note: Prison Architect: build and manage a prison
Cook, Serve, Delicious!: typing-driven restaurant cooking

options.how: You set how many townspeople fill each occupation; they then gather, farm and build on their own.
You put each item on a shelf and set its price yourself, watching customer reactions to adjust.

sources.note: Banished: 20 occupations; townspeople are the main resource
Moonlighter: put items on sale and set their price carefully

options.how: You govern large districts and weigh the interests of factions and population groups, treating citizens as blocs, not characters.
Each duplicant has inborn traits that add or remove attributes; some negative traits bar skills such as digging.

sources.note: Frostpunk 2: maneuver across the interests of many groups, factions and large city districts
Oxygen Not Included: inborn traits give attribute bonuses or penalties and can block skills

options.how: Population is modeled as pop groups with shared economic needs and political desires; you employ labor in bulk, not person by person.
Every ruler and courtier is a character whose traits and lifestyle drive their schemes; genetics pass traits to children.

sources.note: Victoria 3: detailed population groups with their own economic needs and political desires
Crusader Kings III: traits and lifestyle choices determine each character's actions; genetics pass to children

options.how: You meet the needs of your inhabitants through production chains, and factories draw on a workforce rather than on named workers.
Each student has their own personality, wants and needs; clubs, friendships and pastoral care shape their happiness and grades.

sources.note: Anno 1800: fulfil the needs of your inhabitants through production chains; workforce feature for factories
Two Point Campus: explore students' individual personalities, wants and needs

options.how: Population is a station total that new sectors house and employ, with crew trust in the corporation tracked as one shared value.
Each colonist is a unique individual with strengths and flaws; a chief scientist can develop alcoholism and drag the colony down.

sources.note: Ixion: a population to manage; sectors house more population and support new jobs; maintain crew trust
Surviving Mars: each colonist is a unique individual with problems and strengths, such as alcoholism

options.how: Provinces hold development numbers for tax, production and manpower; people are never simulated one by one.
Every ruler and courtier is a character with traits, a dynasty, opinions and ambitions that drive events.

sources.note: Europa Universalis IV: province-based grand strategy
Crusader Kings II: characters and dynasties

options.how: Each scenario sets a target, such as a guest count and park rating, to reach by a deadline.
Sandbox mode drops career objectives, so you design and grow the zoo with no win condition.

sources.note: RollerCoaster Tycoon: scenario-based park building
Planet Zoo: animal welfare, habitats and a sandbox mode

options.how: Each mission sets target ratings for culture, prosperity, peace and favor that you must reach to be promoted.
The main mode has no win condition: you grow the city as large or as strange as you like.

sources.note: Caesar III: a governor career of city missions pleasing the emperor
SimCity 2000: design any city you can imagine

options.how: Each hospital has star ratings to earn; curing one town's patients leads on to a bigger, busier hospital with new challenges.
A sandbox colony builder with no win screen: you see how long your beaver colony lasts through recurring droughts.

sources.note: Two Point Hospital: star goals at each hospital; finishing one leads to a bigger challenge
Timberborn: sandbox city builder; see how long your colony can last through droughts

options.how: Campaign levels each end when you destroy the hero lord or rival keeper of that region.
Fortress mode has no victory: you dig and grow until the fortress falls or you retire it.

sources.note: Dungeon Keeper: heroes come for your gold; dig a dungeon with imps
Dwarf Fortress: dwarves with simulated personalities in a generated world

options.how: Story chapters drive the station toward a set destination; lose the crew's trust in the corporation and you face failure and mutiny.
Free play, with many configuration options, lets you grow a transport network across eras without set missions.

sources.note: Ixion: chapters of story toward reaching a final destination; maintain crew trust or face mutiny
Transport Fever 2: free play with countless configuration possibilities, separate from the campaigns

options.how: The main mode is a multi-chapter story campaign across your tenure as Steward; endless Utopia Builder is a separate mode.
Pick any of hundreds of nations and any start date, then rewrite history with no fixed victory to chase.

sources.note: Frostpunk 2: multi-chapter story campaign; Utopia Builder sandbox with infinite play time
Europa Universalis IV: start at any date with any of hundreds of nations and rewrite history

options.how: Each settlement is won by building reputation before the Scorched Queen's impatience runs out, then you move on to the next.
Every city starts as an empty map with no end goal: you plan it all out or wing it as the city grows.

sources.note: Against the Storm: manage reputation to secure each settlement while the Scorched Queen demands progress
Cities: Skylines II: every city starts as an empty map; plan it all out or wing it
